R392.note: Splits GET (renders a self-contained confirmation form) from a CrossOriginProtection-wrapped POST that performs deletion; complete within the one file, preserves email-link convenience.

R393.note: CRLF/allowlist validation closes the CRLF injection, but the write-up's 'primary recommendation' FTPClient code calls retrieveFile with new FileOutputStream(requestedFileName), writing to an unsanitized attacker-controlled local path - introduces a new path-traversal/arbitrary-file-write weakness.

R394.note: StringSet() via RESP framing cleanly closes delimiter injection, but the constructor signature change (TcpClient to IConnectionMultiplexer) requires updating DI/composition-root code that is not in the case files; disclosed as a required follow-up, so the app won't build/run until that's applied.

R395.note: SandboxedEnvironment is Jinja2's supported mechanism for untrusted templates; call signature and return unchanged, matches the stated contract.

R396.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode() on the text-node message closes reflected XSS with no other observable change.

R397.note: Standard database/sql placeholder parameterization; output identical for legitimate usernames.

R398.note: Hostname/IPv4 allowlist plus escapeshellarg structurally prevents shell metacharacters; minor IPv6 exclusion is not a realistic regression for this ping-reachability check.

R399.note: POST plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken correctly protects the sink, but the write-up explicitly leaves the confirmation view unmodified, so the existing 'Yes, delete' GET link breaks until that view is updated - disclosed but not applied.

R400.note: Control-character exclusion regex blocks CR/LF injection while still permitting ordinary folder names (spaces, punctuation).

R401.note: Textbook save-next-before-free fix; matches the stated contract exactly (freed once, traversal continues, order preserved).

R402.note: RFC4515-style escaping of the special LDAP filter characters (plus a harmless extra slash escape) neutralizes filter injection without altering legitimate matches.

R403.note: CGI::escapeHTML() on both fields closes XSS; priority is restricted to a fixed known-value string so encoding it changes nothing observable.

R404.note: Absolute-path/'..'-prefix rejection plus a separator-aware containment check on the cleaned absolute path blocks traversal without affecting legitimate in-tree reads.

R405.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword with a dummy-hash branch closes both the plaintext comparison and the user-enumeration timing side-channel; states the required password-store migration to hashes.

R406.note: Named parameter carries the full '%term%' pattern as data; standard HQL parameterization, no behavior change for legitimate search.

R407.note: Method-type assertion in keyFunc plus jwt.WithValidMethods(HS256) closes algorithm confusion; legitimate HS256 tokens unaffected.

R408.note: FlaskForm/validate_on_submit() correctly wires CSRF token validation, but the write-up itself notes the template still needs a csrf_token() field it doesn't add - legitimate submissions will fail CSRF validation until that's done.
